{
  "hazard_consequence_node": [
    {
      "label": "HazardConsequence",
      "name": "Dust explosion",
      "node_id": "H1",
      "node_type": "HazardConsequence",
      "evidence": "The case study examines the \"explosion and flash fires\" at US Ink. The report states that \"the ignition led to a dust explosion within the dust collector\" and that this pressure rise then \"triggered an initial flash fire\" and the later larger flash fire/fireball. Witness observations were also described as \"consistent with the sights and sounds of a combustible dust deflagration.\"",
      "explanation": "The main accident mechanism analyzed is spontaneous ignition of combustible dust/sludge in the ductwork, propagation to the dust collector, a dust explosion with suppression-system activation, and then back-propagation that produced the secondary flash-fire sequence. The flash fire caused the injuries, but the dust explosion is the central hazardous phenomenon and primary focus of the technical analysis.",
      "source": "Not specified"
    }
  ],
  "entity_nodes": [
    {
      "label": "Material",
      "name": "Gilsonite, carbon black, and clay dust mixture",
      "node_id": "En1",
      "node_type": "Entity",
      "evidence": "powdery mixture of accumulated carbon black, Gilsonite, and clay in the ductwork of the dust collection system",
      "explanation": "This combustible dust mixture was the principal fuel involved in the duct and dust collector deflagration sequence.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Material",
      "name": "Hydrocarbon oil, clay, and carbon black sludge",
      "node_id": "En2",
      "node_type": "Entity",
      "evidence": "the duct sludge was a mixture of hydrocarbon oil, clay, and carbon black",
      "explanation": "The accumulated sludge-like residue in the ductwork was identified as the material that self-heated and probably ignited first.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Location",
      "name": "Dust collection system ductwork above T-306",
      "node_id": "En3",
      "node_type": "Entity",
      "evidence": "heat charring of the ductwork directly above T-306",
      "explanation": "The investigation concluded that the fire originated in this section of ductwork before propagating to the collector and back through the system.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Location",
      "name": "Dust collector",
      "node_id": "En4",
      "node_type": "Entity",
      "evidence": "the ignition led to a dust explosion within the dust collector",
      "explanation": "The dust explosion occurred in the dust collector, where the suppression system activated and flame propagation then moved back toward the process area.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ],
  "condition_nodes": [
    {
      "label": "Phase",
      "name": "Solid",
      "node_id": "C1",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "powdery mixture of accumulated carbon black, Gilsonite, and clay",
      "explanation": "The hazardous fuel was primarily present as combustible dust/solid particulate in the ductwork and collector.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Pressure",
      "name": "High pressure",
      "node_id": "C2",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "created a pressure spike of 4.4 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) in the dust collector",
      "explanation": "The dust explosion generated an elevated internal pressure in the dust collector.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Temperature",
      "name": "High temperature",
      "node_id": "C3",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "the typical 240°F temperature for the mixing tanks and the maximum 300°F recorded for T-306 and T-106",
      "explanation": "Heated process conditions and self-heating of residues supported the ignition scenario.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Combustibility",
      "name": "Combustible",
      "node_id": "C4",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "consistent with the sights and sounds of a combustible dust deflagration",
      "explanation": "The involved dust/residue was capable of burning rapidly and exploding when dispersed and ignited.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "ReleaseType",
      "name": "Continuous release",
      "node_id": "C5",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "with the system continuing to draw condensable vapors into the duct",
      "explanation": "Material entered and accumulated in the ductwork over several hours of continued system operation rather than from a single sudden discharge.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Confinement",
      "name": "High confinement",
      "node_id": "C6",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "within the dust collector",
      "explanation": "The deflagration occurred inside enclosed process equipment and ducting, which provided strong confinement for pressure development.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "Dispersion",
      "name": "Dispersed",
      "node_id": "C7",
      "node_type": "Condition",
      "evidence": "The residual flame ignited the dispersed dust",
      "explanation": "Airborne dispersed dust was present during the escalation sequence, supporting rapid flame spread and fireball development.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ],
  "event_nodes": [
    {
      "label": "InitiatingEvent",
      "name": "Continuous operation of heated mixing tanks and dust collection system after commissioning",
      "node_id": "Ev1",
      "node_type": "Event",
      "evidence": "The CSB concluded that the explosion and flash fires occurred because of continuous manually controlled heating of the mixing tanks and operation of the dust collection system for several hours after commissioning, with the system continuing to draw condensable vapors into the duct.",
      "explanation": "This was the earliest abnormal operating condition that initiated the accumulation and heating of combustible residues in the ductwork.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "MechanicalFailure",
      "name": "Dust collection system automatic shutdown malfunction",
      "node_id": "Ev2",
      "node_type": "Event",
      "evidence": "the dust collection system actually continued to run overnight, even when all the ink mixers were shut off",
      "explanation": "The new dust collection system failed to shut down as intended, allowing prolonged operation that contributed to residue accumulation and self-heating.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    },
    {
      "label": "IgnitionSource",
      "name": "Spontaneous self-ignition of accumulated sludge in ductwork",
      "node_id": "Ev3",
      "node_type": "Event",
      "evidence": "the incident probably started with the self-heating and spontaneous ignition of the accumulated sludge (mostly Gilsonite and carbon black mixed with hydrocarbon oils) in the ductwork of the dust collection system",
      "explanation": "Self-heated combustible sludge/residue in the ductwork provided the ignition that initiated the explosion and flash-fire sequence.",
      "source": "incident_description"
    }
  ]
}
